Hi Sophie —

Great talking yesterday — thanks again for sharing more about BrightAI's roadmap. Per our call, attached is a concise starter option that many early-stage ML platforms choose when they want predictable spend and capacity without over-committing during product ramp. High level: 2 options we can move forward with quickly.

Option A — 12 month starter (faster time-to-value)
- Upfront: $100,000 prepaid credit applied to usage
- Term discount: 15% off list per-token pricing across eligible models
- Ramped minimums: months 1–3 grace window: 50% of monthly committed baseline; months 4+ month-to-month baseline kicks in
- Ramp credits: unused portion of month 1–3 minimums converted to one-time credits applied to months 4–6 to smooth cost during product launch
- Support: Standard Business SLAs, 1 named SE for onboarding

Option B — 18 month starter (deeper unit economics)
- Upfront: $160,000 prepaid credit
- Term discount: 20% off list
- Ramped minimums: 40% for first month, 60% for months 2–3, baseline months 4+
- Same support and onboarding cadence

I attached a sample ramp schedule (BrightAI_Ramp_Schedule_v3.xlsx) and a draft SOW for scope. If helpful I can sketch the month-by-month expected burn for your initial feature set.

Would you be open to a 30-minute call on Tuesday to pick a direction? If you're ready we can also send a DocuSign with the 12-month starter for signature and make onboarding a high priority.

Thanks,

Thanks for the quick follow-up and the options. A few clarifying Qs before we sync:
1) The 'ramp credits' line — can you show an example numeric scenario? e.g., if we only use 30% of month 1 minimum, how is that converted and applied?
2) For the 12-month option, is the 15% discount applied to all consumption or only to consumption beyond the prepaid credit?
3) Do you have any flexibility on the upfront size? Our CFO prefers keeping cash on the balance sheet; would a $75k upfront with a slightly higher monthly minimum be something you could do for seed-stage customers?

Hi Sophie — thanks — answers inline below and I attached a worked example in the XLS.

1) Ramp credits example (12-month plan):
- Committed monthly baseline assumed for budgeting: $8,333/mo (implied by $100k / 12).
- Month 1 minimum (grace window): 50% => $4,167. If actual usage in month 1 = $1,250, the unused monthly minimum credit = $2,917.
- We convert the unused minimums for months 1–3 into a one-time supplemental credit and apply it to months 4–6. In the example that would reduce months 4–6 by ~$972/mo until exhausted.

2) Discount application: the 15% term discount applies to list pricing for consumption beyond the prepaid credit; prepaid credit consumes at list then discount applies to overage. We can discuss applying a modest pro-rata discount to prepaid credit if you prefer simpler accounting.

3) Flexibility on upfront: we can do a $75k upfront for 12 months if we adjust the ramped minimums upward slightly (e.g., month 1: 60% min, months 2–3: 70%). That keeps the same expected ARR profile for Redwood while giving you a lower cash outlay up-front.

Compliance: attaching our SOC 2 summary and data residency note. Ops, happy to set a technical intake with our security engineer.

If that looks roughly OK, I can draft the final SOW and a DocuSign with the 12-month, $75k upfront variant. Call availability: Tue 11am or Wed 9am PT.

Best,
Camila
